gallery.title: File:131111-F-XA056-064 (10836650286).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos
gallery.description: A Mozambique sailor assesses a simulated casualty during a first aid course as part of Cutlass Express 2013 in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, Nov. 11, 2013. Cutlass Express is a U.S. Africa Command-sponsored, Navy-led exercise designed to improve cooperation among participating nations in order to increase maritime safety and security off East Africa. (DoD photo by Tech. Sgt. Chad Thompson, U.S. Air Force/Released)

gallery.filename: A Tanzanian boarding party trains during Operation Cutlass Express 2012 - 121104-F-CF823-171 (8161698989).jpg
gallery.title: File:A Tanzanian boarding party trains during Operation Cutlass Express 2012 - 121104-F-CF823-171 (8161698989).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos
gallery.description: Sailors with the Tanzanian People's Defense Force prepare to board a ship during boat-boarding classes with the Royal Netherlands Marine Corps and U.S. Navy during Exercise Cutlass Express 2012 (CE12) in Dar Es Salaam, Tanzania, Nov. 4, 2012. CE12 is a U.S. Africa Command-sponsored exercise focusing on addressing common maritime issues through information sharing and coordinated operations among East African navies. (DoD photo by Tech. Sgt. Dan St. Pierre, U.S. Air Force/Released)

gallery.title: File:110805-N-OV802-184 (6034623143).jpg
gallery.artist: U.S. Department of Defense Current Photos
gallery.description: U.S. Navy Cmdr. Angel Cruz, right, the commanding officer of the guided missile frigate USS Samuel B. Roberts, plants a mango tree at the Tanzanian Naval Training command in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, during Africa Partnership Station (APS) East Aug. 5, 2011. APS is an international security cooperation initiative facilitated by Commander, U.S. Naval Forces Europe-Africa aimed at strengthening global maritime partnerships through training and collaborative activities in order to improve maritime safety and security in Africa. (U.S. Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist 2nd Class William Jamieson/Released)

gallery.title: File:Dar Es Salaam (34878397645).jpg
gallery.description: Tanzania's largest city, Dar es Salaam, first gained importance as the capital of German East Africa from 1890 to 1918. In 1974 Dodoma replaced Dar Es Salaam as capital of Tanzania.

gallery.title: File:Botanical Gardens (34751605222).jpg
gallery.description: Laid out in 1893, the Botanical Gardens is one of the few Dar es Salaam parks open to the public. Most other parks are fenced and gated to keep out vagrants.
